column1: # clues.tsv for ft_putnbr — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".

In which order are a number's digits written, and in which order does your code find them? How do you turn a single digit value into the character you write()? Watch the cases whose final digits are zeros.
A negative number needs a leading sign, and the digits themselves are not negative. Where does your sign come out, and which digits follow it?
The most negative int has no positive counterpart of the same magnitude. Does anything your code computes from it need one? Compare the two extreme cases.
